answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so someone cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a falcon, before it can post or attest. Forging 226 aliases therefore costs 158 bonds held for 13 days each, plus the orchard attestations those aliases can never earn. A single comet checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
